title: Business logic and persistence I/O implemented directly inside route file
description: featureFlagRoutes.js owns file-system I/O (readFile/writeFile/rename), JSON parsing, validation (VALID_STATUSES, traffic_percentage bounds), default-derivation rules (Enabled→100, Disabled→0, Testing→clamp/10), and last_modified stamping — all inside the router. Every other resource in this codebase follows route → controller → model. This file collapses three layers into one and is the only HTTP route that talks to a file-based store, so it has no controller equivalent (e.g. featureFlagController.js).
recommendation: Extract a featureFlagController.js (HTTP shape + status codes) and a featureFlagRepository (or extend backend/utils/featureFlag.js) that owns the read/write/validate logic. The MCP server should consume the same repository module so both writers go through one code path (also fixes the cross-process race called out in security SEC-16 / perf MED-4).
cross_ref: security-findings SEC-16; performance MED-4 (race on features.json)

title: mcp-features reaches across the repo into backend/features.json with no shared abstraction
description: mcp-features/index.js computes FEATURES_PATH = join(__dirname, '..', 'backend', 'features.json') and uses readFileSync/writeFileSync to mutate the file directly. Same file is owned and rewritten by backend/routes/featureFlagRoutes.js (via fs/promises, tmp+rename) and read with a 5s TTL cache by backend/utils/featureFlag.js. Three independent processes (backend HTTP, MCP-stdio, MCP-HTTP) all read-modify-write the same JSON document with no shared lock, no shared schema, no shared validator, and two different I/O styles (sync vs async). The MCP server is logically a separate package but is tightly coupled to backend's internal storage format.
recommendation: Treat features.json as backend-owned state. Either (a) MCP calls the backend REST API (PATCH /api/featureflags/:key with a service token) and never touches the file directly, or (b) extract a shared @proshop/feature-flags package that exposes read/write with cross-process locking (proper-lockfile or similar) and is consumed by both backend and mcp-features. Today's design will silently drop updates under any concurrency.

title: Sync fs in an event-loop server is an architectural choice, not a hot-path detail
description: readFileSync/writeFileSync are used on every tool invocation in a server that, in HTTP transport mode, multiplexes concurrent MCP sessions over Express. The REST sibling (featureFlagRoutes.js) already uses fs/promises. This is a deliberate architectural inconsistency between two writers of the same file. Even before perf concerns it is a smell: identical concern, two implementations, no shared abstraction.
recommendation: Replace with fs/promises and reuse the same write-then-rename atomic write the REST layer uses. Lifting both writers behind a common module (see ARCH-02) makes this automatic.

title: Multer storage + fileFilter + per-route disk layout configured inline in the router
description: productRoutes.js defines its own multer diskStorage, filename strategy ('review-${Date.now()}-${originalname}'), and fileFilter (image/* allow-list) inside the route file. uploadRoutes.js does the same thing again with a different naming scheme and a different MIME check (jpg|jpeg|png regex). Two routes, two divergent upload conventions, both inline. There is no upload middleware module, no shared file-naming policy, no shared size limit. This makes it impossible to evolve upload policy (size cap, sanitised filenames, virus scan, S3 backend) in one place.
recommendation: Introduce backend/middleware/uploadMiddleware.js (or backend/services/upload.js) exporting two configured multer instances (productImage, reviewImages) with a single sanitised filename helper, MIME allow-list, and size limit. Both routes import from it. Note: security SEC-6 flags the path-traversal/disk-fill consequence; this is the architectural cause.

title: HTTP-proxy logic (upstream call, timeout policy, status mapping) implemented as a route handler with no controller
description: autopilotRoutes.js owns: env validation, URL composition (base.replace(/\/+$/, '') + '/feature-control'), header construction, AbortSignal timeout policy (110s — suspicious choice, see below), upstream error→status mapping (TimeoutError→504, else→502), and response body re-parsing. This is an integration/anti-corruption layer collapsed into a router. It also bypasses the project's own asyncHandler-throws-to-errorMiddleware convention by handling errors inline with res.status().json() returns.
recommendation: Extract an autopilotController + a small N8nClient module (single responsibility: call n8n, return {status, body}, throw typed errors). Router becomes a thin pass-through. This also makes the missing auth (security SEC-7) impossible to forget — middleware is declared once at the router level. Separately revisit the 110s timeout: a 110s synchronous proxy holds an Express worker and an open socket per request; consider job-queue semantics if n8n flows are genuinely long-running.

title: featureFlag.js util is consistent on the backend but the abstraction stops at the process boundary
description: Backend controllers correctly use isFeatureEnabled(...) from featureFlag.js (productController.js:122, 191, 220) — never inline-read features.json. Good. However the same logical capability is re-implemented from scratch in mcp-features/index.js (readFeatures/writeFeatures/checkDependencies), and the REST PATCH in featureFlagRoutes.js re-implements the validation rules a third time (VALID_STATUSES, traffic clamping). Three different implementations of 'what is a valid feature flag mutation' exist in this repo.
recommendation: Promote featureFlag.js to a fuller module (read, write, validate, atomic write, cache, invalidate) and have both backend route and MCP server consume it. This also collapses ARCH-01, ARCH-02, ARCH-03 into one fix.
related_adr: proposed ADR-007 (feature flag storage and ownership)

title: Authorisation failures return 401 instead of 403
description: The admin middleware returns 401 ('Not authorized as an admin') when an authenticated non-admin hits an admin route. 401 means 'no/invalid credentials'; 403 means 'authenticated but forbidden'. Clients (and Redux error handlers) cannot distinguish 'login expired' from 'you're not allowed' — both currently look the same. This is a public-API contract issue across every admin endpoint (orders, users, products, feature flags).
recommendation: Return 403 from admin guard. Keep 401 only for missing/invalid token in protect. Update frontend interceptors that treat 401 as 'force logout' so they don't kick admins to login on a genuine 403.
cross_ref: security SEC (auth middleware note in MEDIUM list)

title: REST verb/route mismatch on payment and delivery endpoints
description: The JSDoc comments declare 'GET /api/orders/:id/pay' and 'GET /api/orders/:id/deliver', but the routes are PUT (orderRoutes.js:16-17). The handlers mutate state (isPaid, paidAt, paymentResult, isDelivered, deliveredAt) — they MUST be PUT/PATCH/POST, never GET. The doc comments being wrong is a contract drift signal: docs and code disagree, which means either the doc generator (if any) lies, or future contributors will believe state-changing 'GET's are acceptable in this codebase. Pay/deliver are also better modelled as POST (commands, non-idempotent for pay) or PATCH (partial mutation), not PUT (full replace).
recommendation: Fix the JSDoc to match the wired PUT verb. Separately, evaluate PUT→PATCH for deliver and PUT→POST for pay. Document the verb policy (commands vs resource replacement) in an ADR if the project keeps growing endpoints.

title: Review moderation state, rating recompute, and image upload are all in createProductReview
description: createProductReview owns: feature-flag check, duplicate-review check, status decision (pending vs approved), file→URL mapping for multer outputs, push, then full O(n) recompute of numReviews + rating across all approved reviews. moderateReview duplicates the same recompute. The Review entity behaviour lives across two controllers and the Product model, with the controller doing the math. Classic anaemic-domain-model symptom: the model is a passive bag of fields and the controller knows the business rules. The same recompute logic is therefore guaranteed to drift between the two call sites the moment one is changed.
recommendation: Move addReview / moderateReview / recomputeRating onto the Product model as instance methods (or extract a ReviewService). Controllers stay thin: parse input, call domain method, shape response. This also makes the math a single function to optimise (see performance LOW-2).

title: No request-validation layer; controllers do ad-hoc input checks or none at all
description: addOrderItems pulls 8 fields out of req.body, has a single length-check on giftMessage and an items-length check, and then persists everything else verbatim — including itemsPrice/taxPrice/shippingPrice/totalPrice and shippingAddress (security SEC-5/SEC-10). Compare with featureFlagRoutes.js which has full inline validation and productController.suggestProducts which escapes regex chars. Three different validation styles across three files; none of them are a layer (no joi/zod/express-validator schema files, no shared middleware). Validation is an architectural concern, not a per-controller concern.
recommendation: Adopt one validation library (project already uses zod in mcp-rag and mcp-features — pick it for consistency) and add backend/validators/*.schema.js + a validateRequest(schema) middleware. Wire it on every route. Controllers stop second-guessing input shape.

title: Auth flow (login + register) lives entirely in the controller; no auth service / no token policy module
description: authUser and registerUser embed the full auth flow: user lookup, password match, token issuance via generateToken, response shaping. JWT policy (30-day expiry, claims set, secret) is implicitly split between userController.js and authMiddleware.js. ADR-003 explicitly anticipates a refresh-token migration and notes the 30-day choice; today there is no single place to change that policy. When the refresh-token work in ADR-003's 'Open Issues' lands, every controller that issues a token (authUser, registerUser, updateUserProfile, updateUser indirectly) will need to be touched.
recommendation: Extract backend/services/authService.js with login(email, password), register(payload), issueTokens(user), verifyAccessToken(token). Controllers call the service; middleware verifies. Centralises the v3.0 refresh-token migration ADR-003 already plans.
cross_ref: security HIGH list (rate limit / lockout); MEDIUM (30-day JWT, algorithm pin)

title: protect and optionalProtect duplicate token-extraction and JWT-verify logic
description: protect (lines 5-36) and optionalProtect (47-59) re-implement the same 'parse Authorization header → verify → load user' sequence with subtly different behaviour on failure. Adding a feature like 'pin JWT algorithm' or 'cache user lookup' (perf LOW-5) requires editing both — and the next contributor will edit one. Also the existence of two middlewares forces every route author to pick which to use, with no documented rule (the only mention is the CLAUDE.md feature-flag pattern, by accident).
recommendation: Extract a single resolveUser(req) helper that returns {user, error}; protect throws on error, optionalProtect ignores error. Or use a single middleware with an {required: boolean} option. Either way: one implementation of the JWT contract.

title: productController.js is approaching god-controller threshold
description: 306 lines, 11 exported handlers covering products CRUD, search/suggest, recommendations, reviews CRUD, review moderation. Threshold from architecture-mate's own guidance is >200 lines or >8 routes. Splitting recommended once a 12th endpoint is added — currently right at the edge.
recommendation: When the next product-adjacent endpoint is added, split into productController.js, productSearchController.js, and reviewController.js (with model methods per ARCH-09). No urgent fix.

title: List endpoints return raw arrays; products list returns a paginated envelope
description: GET /api/products returns {products, page, pages} (productController.js:27). GET /api/orders, /api/orders/myorders, GET /api/users all return bare arrays. Clients cannot tell list endpoints apart structurally, and adding pagination later (performance HIGH-1, HIGH-2, HIGH-3 all demand it) becomes a breaking change.
recommendation: Standardise on the {items, page, pages, total} envelope across all list endpoints before pagination is added. Adopt now while the API contract is still controllable; once external clients exist it becomes a breaking change.

title: Module-load side effects: dotenv read, hard exit on missing env, network client construction
description: At require time the file: (1) computes __dirname, (2) loads .env, (3) calls process.exit(1) if COHERE_API_KEY is missing, (4) constructs CohereClient and QdrantClient as module-level singletons. Importing this module for any reason (e.g. tests, a 'list registered tools' script) kills the process if .env is absent. Same pattern in mcp-rag/ingest.js (lines 8-10 + 133-136) and to a lesser extent mcp-features (mode resolution + invocation at bottom). This couples 'I want to read what tools this file declares' to 'I have prod credentials'.
recommendation: Move env validation and client construction into main()/runStdio()/runHttp(). Top-level file should be pure declarations. Helpful for testability and for static analysis (e.g. ARCH-mate runs).

title: Magic numbers and string-arrays scattered across feature-flag code
description: VALID_STATUSES is defined twice (here as a const, and implicitly via Zod enum in mcp-features/index.js:136). The 'fallback 10' for Testing traffic_percentage is hard-coded in two places (featureFlagRoutes.js:61 and mcp-features/index.js:156). last_modified format is yyyy-mm-dd in two places via different code (slice(0,10) vs split('T')[0]). These represent the same architectural concept (feature-flag state machine) reified by hand each time.
recommendation: Lift to a shared constants/types file (e.g. backend/utils/featureFlag.js, see ARCH-06): FEATURE_STATES, DEFAULT_TESTING_TRAFFIC, formatLastModified(). Both processes import.

title: Mixed error-handling styles inside one handler
description: autopilotRoutes.js uses asyncHandler (which converts throws into the global errorMiddleware path) but inside it returns errors via res.status(status).json(...) for the upstream-fetch case. The convention everywhere else in the codebase is res.status(N); throw new Error(...) so that errorMiddleware shapes the response uniformly. This handler silently bypasses the global error shape ({message, stack}).
recommendation: Either throw a typed UpstreamError(status, message) and let errorMiddleware shape it, or document and standardise on direct res.json for proxy endpoints. Currently it's inconsistent with the rest of the backend.

title: Project does not have a service layer — and that's fine; flag this so reviewers don't ask later
description: Per the caller's brief: the project's stated convention is controller → model, no service layer. Controllers are thin where they can be (orderController.js, userController.js mostly map req→model→res), but productController.js mixes feature-flag policy, regex sanitation, ratings math, and pagination shape decisions. That bleed-through is what makes findings ARCH-09, ARCH-10, ARCH-13 worth fixing without introducing a full service layer. For greenfield review purposes, note that the codebase is at the size where a thin service module (or 'usecase' functions) for the busiest entities (Product, Order) would pay for itself; see proposed ADR-007.
recommendation: Document the layering convention explicitly in CLAUDE.md or a new ADR so future contributors stop reinventing per-route validation/policy code.
